content.title: Opening Day chaos in Houston comes with price: $80 parking stuns fans
content.text: LAM Parking at 1603 Rusk St. ahead of Opening Day for the Houston Astros' 2026 season. Leah Vann/Chron.comDowntown Houston will be buzzing all weekend as multiple sports events and conventions take over the city, but good luck finding affordable parking, if you can find a spot at all. Thursday will be the busiest day of all: the Houston Astros are hosting the Los Angeles Angels on Opening Day at 3:10 p.m. at Daikin Park, while the NCAA South Regional will start its first of two games at 6:30 p.m. at Toyota Center.Article continues below this adAs a result, independently owned lots have raised their usual prices to as high as $70 and $80 as of Thursday morning. The initial game between Nebraska and Iowa will draw many Midwesterners, some of whom avoided airport security lines by driving 13-17 hours to Houston for a historic rivalry matchup. It's Nebraska's first trip to the Sweet 16 of NCAA Men's March Madness, while it's Iowa's first time in 27 years. Meanwhile, the later game will feel like a home game as the Houston Cougars will tip off against the Illinois Fighting Illini at 9 p.m.Winners of tonight's games will advance to the Elite 8 round on Saturday, meaning some traveling fanbases will be here to stay. The Astros will keep their opening weekend going with the Angels in a four-game series, featuring evening games on Friday and Saturday, and an afternoon game on Sunday. Moreover, two major conventions are being held in Downtown Houston. CERAWeek—a premier annual energy conference often called the "Super Bowl of energy" is currently being held from March 23-27 at various downtown locations. In addition, Creapure HYROX brings the World Series of Fitness Racing back to Houston at the George R. Brown Convention Center from March 26-29.Article continues below this adAmid the chaos, traveling to and from downtown will be a challenge; figuring out where to park will be an entirely different matter (pun intended). While the Astros confirmed that their usual lot prices will remain the same, some city-owned lots around the Toyota Center will see prices fluctuate based on demand throughout the weekend. LAM Parking at the intersection of Rusk St. and Chartres St. ahead of Opening Day for the Houston Astros' 2026 season. Leah Vann/Chron.comLAM Parking has raised its prices beyond those established by Daikin Park and Toyota Center. These surface lots received complaints from fans last year due to costs reaching up to $80 per parking spot, including one located at 1603 Rusk Street. Typically, these spots range from $10 to $60, depending on parking duration and location.LAM manages over 40 surface lots in downtown Houston near Daikin Park, the George R. Brown Convention Center, and the Toyota Center. These lots might fill up quickly depending on the price, because it's not only Opening Day and the NCAA South Regional, but also Houston's HYROX race, which is expected to bring 2,000 competitors to the convention center throughout the weekend. This number doesn't include the friends and family they will bring. Article continues below this adStill, these surface lots are clearly taking advantage of the weekend. Despite being farther from both Daikin Park and Toyota Center, the elevated prices will make them the last spots remaining after all the cheaper ones are taken. Any other @Astros fans coming to the game: warning that the parking anywhere close to the Daikin park is $60 up; so we found a place in that church Garage on Texas Avenue and San Jacinto that is only $25.— Michael Beckman (@michaelbeck) March 26, 2026 For comparison, here's a list of parking costs in downtown Houston for the weekend.Daikin Park Parking (Houston Astros)Article continues below this ad Diamond Lot - $60 Lot A - $50 Lot B - $40 Lot C - $30 Toyota Center Parking (Houston Rockets, NCAA Tournament) Tundra - $45 Avenida South - $50 Central - $35 North - $45 Article continues below this adPricing for the Tundra and Avenida South garages will depend on the mix of teams competing in the NCAA Sweet 16 and the corresponding demand, a Houston First spokesperson told Chron. The best case for any fan, convention-attendee or HYROX competitor is to get to their events as early as possible. Or just take an Uber. March 26, 2026Leah Vann is a sports culture reporter covering the Houston Astros, college football and notable Houston-area athletes. The Fort Worth-native is a graduate of both the University of Texas at Austin and Northwestern University. She most recently worked as an LSU beat writer for The Advocate, covering the baseball team's run to a College World Series title behind MLB first-round draft picks Dylan Crews and Paul Skenes. Her work has also appeared in NBC News THINK, Baseball America, The Sunday Long Read, Fort Worth Star-Telegram, The Dallas Morning News and The Forward.
